## Vocabulary

- **self**: Cloud HSM Atlas (14/3)

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Cloud HSM documents an 8 KiB message-size limit and separate HSM quota usage. Atlas’s key-wrapping design means these operations concern encryption keys rather than whole database files. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md
- [statement] Cloud HSM documentation limits user-provided plaintext/ciphertext plus additional authenticated data to 8 KiB, versus 64 KiB for software keys. This API message limit should not be interpreted as an Atlas document-size limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Google’s September 2022 encryption matrix explicitly lists MongoDB Atlas with Cloud KMS and CloudHSM support. MongoDB’s shared responsibility model also includes HSM-backed customer-managed keys. (high confidence) (verified as of 2022-09-16) — https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/inside-google-cloud/architecting-for-database-encryption-on-google-cloud · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas · also: https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/fundamentals/shared-responsibility, https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm
- [statement] Cloud HSM exposes hardware-backed cryptographic operations through Cloud KMS. Google manages the HSM cluster, including scaling and patching. (high confidence) — https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas · also: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/inside-google-cloud/architecting-for-database-encryption-on-google-cloud
- [statement] Atlas uses the Google Cloud customer-managed key to wrap per-node MongoDB master keys; those master keys wrap per-database encryption keys used by WiredTiger. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas
- [statement] For the documented integration, create a symmetric encrypt/decrypt key with HSM protection in Cloud KMS, then supply its fully qualified CryptoKeyVersion resource name to Atlas and grant the Atlas identity the required key permissions. (medium confidence) — https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md
- [statement] The Atlas Google Cloud KMS guide requires M10 or larger clusters, Project Owner access, project-level configuration, and subsequent enablement on each target cluster; Free and Flex clusters are excluded. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas
- [statement] Atlas does not automatically rotate its configured Google Cloud Key Version Resource ID. Update Atlas after key rotation, and retain the old version until changes deploy and no retained snapshot needs it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas
- [statement] MongoDB warns that revoking Atlas access to its customer-managed key shuts down cluster nodes and makes data inaccessible until key access is restored. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas
- [statement] Treat key storage, least-privilege access, rotation, and recovery as operational responsibilities. Percona recommends dedicated KMS or HSM storage and key lifecycle controls; MongoDB assigns customer-managed key configuration and access policies to customers. (high confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/securing-your-mongodb-database-essential-best-practices/ · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas · also: https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/fundamentals/shared-responsibility
- [statement] Google describes Cloud HSM as a managed cluster of FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified HSMs; Google manages clustering, scaling and patching. This certification statement concerns the HSM service, not a certification of an entire Atlas deployment. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas · also: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/inside-google-cloud/architecting-for-database-encryption-on-google-cloud
- [statement] Atlas requires an M10-or-larger cluster, a symmetric KMS key and its fully qualified CryptoKeyVersion resource ID. Configure customer key management for the project, then enable it on each intended cluster. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas
- [statement] Revoking Atlas access to its customer-managed key can shut down cluster nodes. Keep the original key version enabled until rotation deploys and no retained backup snapshot needs it. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas
- [statement] Google documents creation of a symmetric HSM key with gcloud kms keys create, --purpose encryption and --protection-level hsm; Atlas separately requires the resulting key-version resource identifier. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm · keywords: Cloud HSM Atlas · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-gcp-kms.md
